subject: history
topicDisplay: Hl Regional Option History Of Asia Oceania
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which year did Lenin die, opening the succession struggle?
questions.explain: Lenin died in January 1924, after which Stalin and Trotsky vied for leadership.

questions.q: In which month and year did the monarchy fall in the February Revolution?
questions.explain: The February Revolution of 1917, in early March by the Western calendar, led to Nicholas II's abdication.

questions.q: In which year did the People's Republic of China take over China's seat at the United Nations from Taiwan?
questions.explain: The PRC replaced Taiwan in the UN, including the Security Council seat, in 1971.

questions.q: In which year did Soviet forces crush the Hungarian Uprising?
questions.explain: The Hungarian Uprising of 1956 was suppressed by Soviet tanks, ousting reformer Imre Nagy.

questions.q: Which wealthier peasants were targeted for 'liquidation' during collectivisation?
questions.explain: The kulaks, supposedly prosperous peasants, were branded class enemies and dekulakised.

questions.q: The 'Gang of Four', the radical clique influential in the late Cultural Revolution, was led by which of Mao's associates?
questions.explain: Jiang Qing, Mao's wife, led the Gang of Four alongside Zhang Chunqiao, Yao Wenyuan and Wang Hongwen.

questions.q: What 1947 US policy pledged support to nations resisting communism?
questions.explain: The Truman Doctrine of 1947 promised aid to free peoples resisting subjugation, starting with Greece and Turkey.

questions.q: The First Five-Year Plan, which prioritised heavy industry on the Soviet model, ran over which period?
questions.explain: The First Five-Year Plan ran from 1953 to 1957 and emphasised Soviet-style heavy industrialisation.

questions.q: In which year did Germany invade the USSR in Operation Barbarossa?
questions.explain: Operation Barbarossa, the German invasion of the Soviet Union, began on 22 June 1941.

questions.q: The Cultural Revolution, Mao's campaign to renew revolutionary fervour, was launched in which year?
questions.explain: The Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution was launched in 1966.

questions.q: Who succeeded Mao as head of state and, with Deng Xiaoping, led pragmatic recovery after the Great Leap famine?
questions.explain: Liu Shaoqi became head of state in 1959 and, with Deng Xiaoping, implemented economic recovery measures.

questions.q: Alexander II became known by which epithet for his early reforms?
questions.explain: For emancipating the serfs and other reforms Alexander II was dubbed the 'Tsar Liberator'.

questions.q: By what name did Russians call World War II on the Eastern Front?
questions.explain: The 1941-45 conflict with Nazi Germany is known in Russia as the Great Patriotic War.

questions.q: In which years was the Korean War fought?
questions.explain: The Korean War lasted from 1950 to the armistice of 1953.

questions.q: Stalin's first Five-Year Plan, launched in 1928, prioritised what?
questions.explain: The first Five-Year Plan (1928-32) emphasised heavy industry such as coal, steel and machinery.

questions.q: Which ideological doctrine did Stalin champion against Trotsky?
questions.explain: Stalin advanced 'Socialism in One Country' against Trotsky's 'Permanent Revolution'.

questions.q: In which month did the Bolsheviks seize power in 1917?
questions.explain: The Bolsheviks took power in the October Revolution of 1917 (early November by the Western calendar).

questions.q: China intervened in the Korean War in support of North Korea in which year?
questions.explain: Chinese 'People's Volunteers' entered the Korean War in October 1950 after UN forces approached the Yalu River.

questions.q: What policy of forced cultural assimilation did Alexander III intensify?
questions.explain: Alexander III pursued Russification, imposing Russian language and Orthodoxy on minority nationalities.

questions.q: The 1950 Marriage Law in the PRC is significant for doing what for women?
options: Outlawing arranged marriage and granting the right to divorce
questions.explain: The 1950 Marriage Law banned arranged marriages and concubinage and gave women the right to divorce.

questions.q: The Hundred Flowers Campaign, encouraging intellectuals to voice criticism, mainly took place in which year?
questions.explain: The Hundred Flowers Campaign reached its height in 1957 before being abruptly reversed.

questions.q: The 'Three-Anti' and 'Five-Anti' campaigns of the early 1950s targeted whom?
options: Corruption among officials and the urban bourgeoisie
questions.explain: The 1951-52 campaigns attacked corruption, waste and bureaucracy among officials and capitalist businessmen.

questions.q: Which reactionary tutor heavily influenced Alexander III's policies?
questions.explain: Pobedonostsev, Procurator of the Holy Synod, championed autocracy, Orthodoxy and Russification under Alexander III.

questions.q: Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China in which year?
questions.explain: Mao proclaimed the PRC from Tiananmen Square on 1 October 1949 after the Communist victory in the civil war.

questions.q: The 1987 INF Treaty between the superpowers eliminated which weapons?
questions.explain: The 1987 Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty scrapped a whole class of land-based missiles.

questions.q: Which Soviet economic body answered the Marshall Plan?
questions.explain: Comecon (1949) coordinated the economies of the Soviet bloc as a counter to Marshall aid.

questions.q: The Brezhnev Doctrine asserted the right to do what?
options: Intervene in any socialist state threatening communism
questions.explain: The Brezhnev Doctrine (1968) claimed the right to intervene to protect socialism in bloc states.

questions.q: What event of 22 January 1905 triggered the 1905 Revolution?
questions.explain: On Bloody Sunday troops fired on peaceful petitioners led by Father Gapon at the Winter Palace.

questions.q: Which 1979 event helped trigger the 'Second Cold War'?
options: The fall of the Berlin Wall
questions.explain: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979 ended detente and heightened tensions.

questions.q: In what year did Stalin die, paving the way for new leadership?
questions.explain: Stalin died in March 1953, beginning a power struggle eventually won by Khrushchev.
